editorial:
You follow two homicide detectives in a rain-soaked city as they chase a killer who turns the seven deadly sins into brutal crime scenes. One is tired and close to retirement, while the other is eager and quick to anger. Their uneasy partnership gives the story real tension, and the film pulls you into a grim world where every clue feels heavy. It is not a light watch, but it keeps you locked in from the first scene.

The acting is strong, especially the quiet detective work and the shocking final stretch. The pacing builds slowly at first, then speeds up as the case tightens, and the dark look fits the story well. The downside is that some scenes are very intense and disturbing, so it is not for everyone. If you enjoy serious crime stories with a big twist, this is a must-see.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the killer surrenders and leads the detectives to a remote spot. A box arrives, and inside is the head of Mills' pregnant wife. The killer explains he was jealous of Mills' life and wanted to make him angry enough to kill him. Mills shoots the killer, completing the seven sins with wrath. Somerset is left to carry on, shaken but alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark crime thrillers with a big twist.
